description: The combat module’s decision, pinned for fixed inputs (US-4 of 120-combat-and-stamina). Each case carries the WHOLE input — both combatants, the authored action row, the fully resolved CombatTuning, the scalar separation, the seed and the tick — so a harness in any language reproduces it with no defaults table, no world file and no KB. `kind` is which entry point the case runs: `attack` is resolveAttack, `defense` is resolveDefense, and they are two doors onto ONE action vocabulary (a dodge is a row with a `defense` profile, a ranged attack is a row with `delivery: projectile`). The two things core cannot know arrive as inputs exactly as they do at runtime: `legality` is the KB’s can_attack/2 answer and `lineOfFire` is the host’s ITrajectoryProbe reading. `expected.resolution` is the AttackResolution/DefenseResolution, `expected.facts` is the { retract, assert } delta it becomes in the 110 predicate vocabulary (combat/combat-facts.ts) — empty for an attack that was never made — and `expected.threat`, where present, is threatAfterDamage accumulated onto `threatBefore`. Rolls are derived from (seed, tick, attacker, defender, action, phase) mixed FNV-1a → mulberry32, one stream per phase, never a shared RNG. Regenerate with `npm run combat-corpus`.

cases.name: melee-hit-flat-tuning
cases.note: The base case, and the one every other reads against: a sword swing with variance, crits and baseline evasion all authored to zero, so the damage IS the weapon’s `item_damage/2` and an assertion about health is an assertion about health.

cases.name: melee-hit-with-variance-and-a-critical
cases.note: The whole damage pipeline under the authored tuning: base → variance → critical → type → block → armour, every stage in `breakdown`. A port that agrees on the total by getting the variance and the critical wrong in opposite directions fails here.

cases.name: melee-miss-the-swing-that-did-not-connect
cases.note: Accuracy is a gate the derived stream answers, not a subtraction from damage. The swing happened — it cost its stamina and it started a fight — and it moved no health. The roll comes from (seed, tick, attacker, defender, action, `accuracy`), so a port that advances one RNG per attack reproduces the hit cases and fails this one.

cases.name: ranged-hit-with-a-clear-line
cases.note: A crossbow bolt is the same row type a sword swing is: `delivery: projectile` and a long `range` are the whole of "ranged" (US-3). The host answered `clear: true` and therefore changed nothing — the damage, the reach and the cost were all core’s.

cases.name: ranged-blocked-line-is-a-miss-not-a-new-outcome
cases.note: THE ranged case. The host said a pillar is in the way; core decided what that MEANS — the bolt was loosed, it cost what it costs, and it is in the wall. The reason is `line_blocked` whatever the host named as the obstruction, because a corpus case pins an atom and `pillar` is scenery. An implementation that invented a `blocked` outcome, or that refunded the stamina, fails here.

cases.name: a-melee-row-never-consults-the-line-of-fire
cases.note: The same blocked reading as the case above, on a `contact` row: nothing obstructs a sword, and the hit lands. `delivery` is the only thing that makes the host’s answer relevant, which is what keeps a melee attack from ever asking a question core does not need.

cases.name: out-of-reach-costs-nothing
cases.note: Reach is the action’s range, else the weapon’s `item_range/2`, against a SCALAR separation in the world’s authored distance unit — core performs no vector math and knows no handedness, unit scale or up-axis. Walking up to something you cannot reach is not a swing, so `staminaSpent` is zero while `staminaCost` still reports the price.

cases.name: dodged-an-open-evasion-window-turns-the-blow-aside
cases.note: The dodge case on the ATTACK side: an actor mid-sidestep is a defender with a `dodgeBonus`, and the blow comes out `dodged` through the ordinary gate. There is no defensive code path in the resolution at all — which is why `resolveDefense` could be added without touching this one.

cases.name: mitigation-resistance-a-raised-guard-and-armour
cases.note: The mitigation case: `resists_damage/2` halves it, `blockReduction` halves what is left, and `armor_value/2` comes off flat at the end. Three different kinds of reduction in one pipeline, in the one order four engines must share — a port that applies armour before the block gets a different number and fails here.

cases.name: vulnerability-multiplies-where-resistance-divides
cases.note: The other half of `damageType`, and the reason the type stage is its own line in `breakdown`: the same swing against a target `vulnerable_to(slashing)` is multiplied by the authored `vulnerableMultiplier`. Neither multiplier is a compiled constant; both are the world’s.

cases.name: exhausted-a-swing-that-could-not-be-paid-for
cases.note: The exhaustion case. The attacker’s `energy/3` is below the action’s `action/4` EnergyCost, so there was no swing: no health moved, no fight started, no stamina left the meter, and the fact delta is empty. It is its own outcome and not a `refused` with a reason, because "too spent to lift the sword" is a thing a world shows a player and an AI reacts to.

cases.name: death-a-lethal-blow-at-zero-health
cases.note: The death case, and the transition the rest of the simulation observes: `alive/1` is retracted and `incapacitated/1` asserted, the corpse leaves `in_combat/1` and stops being anybody’s `combat_target/2`. The lifecycle facts a death also owes (`deceased/3`, `cause_of_death/2`) belong to the decision layer, not to the pure resolution, and are asserted by `CombatResolver` — so a port reproduces this delta and adds those two.

cases.name: subdual-zero-health-without-a-death
cases.note: The same blow from an action authored `lethal: false`. The target is `incapacitated/1` and still `alive/1` — which is what a duelling, sparring or arrest mechanic is, authored rather than coded. A world that sets `deathAtZero: false` gets this for every action.

cases.name: refused-a-forbidden-attack-does-not-resolve
cases.note: THE negative case, and the one that stops the corpus passing vacuously. The rules layer answered `can_attack/2` false, so the attack did not happen: no damage, no health movement, no `in_combat/1`, no stamina spent, and an EMPTY fact delta. An implementation that resolves a forbidden attack "for zero damage" passes every other case in this file and fails this one — permission is a gate, not a modifier.

cases.name: refused-a-downed-target-is-not-a-legal-target
cases.note: State is a gate of its own, checked after legality and before everything else: an `incapacitated/1` defender cannot be attacked even where the rules layer permits it. Same empty delta, different reason — two refusals a harness must keep distinguishable.

cases.name: dodge-opens-a-window-the-host-will-time
cases.note: The dodge case on the DEFENSIVE side. What core decides: that the window opens, how wide the evasion is, what `has_status/3` atom the actor wears, and what it cost. What core does NOT decide: when it closes. `window` and `recovery` are authored time handed to the host — there is no clock, no tick and no expiry anywhere in the pinned output, and a port that added one would have nothing here to reproduce it against.

cases.name: a-row-with-no-defense-profile-is-not-a-dodge
cases.note: The negative case for the defensive path: the sword swing put through `resolveDefense` is refused with `not_a_defense` and an empty delta. "Dodge" is not a kind of action in code — it is a row that authored an evasion — so the check is for the DATA and not for an id, a category or a flag.

cases.name: dodge-exhausted-out-of-the-same-meter-a-swing-is-paid-from
cases.note: One shared resource, proven at the boundary: the actor who cannot pay for a swing cannot pay for a sidestep either, out of the same `energy/3` and through the same `action/4` cost column. A world where dodging had its own pool would resolve this `evading`.
